title: ASP.NET Core platform model and framework choices
concepts: ASP.NET Core is Microsoft's cross-platform web framework on .NET. It provides hosting, HTTP abstractions, middleware, routing, dependency injection integration, configuration and logging; application styles such as APIs, MVC and interactive web UI build on these foundations.

An ASP.NET Core process starts a host, composes services and a request pipeline, and listens through a server such as Kestrel. The server receives HTTP; middleware and selected endpoints implement application behavior.

Framework comparisons should begin with requirements: language and team experience, deployment target, ecosystem libraries, concurrency and workload shape, security support, operational tooling, and long-term maintenance.

ASP.NET Core, Node.js with Express, Spring Boot, and Django are not interchangeable feature lists. They have different language runtimes, conventions, ecosystems, and hosting models; each can build web services and each still needs sound architecture and operations.

Use the current supported .NET release for new work unless compatibility or hosting constraints require another target. As of the source check, .NET 11 is the current STS release and .NET 10 remains the current LTS release. Both are actively supported; choose according to support horizon and target platform.
